```{python}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
import pickle
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Created by scripts/01_clean_data.py and scripts/02_analysis.py: run those first
root = Path(".")
results_path = root / "output" / "results.pkl"

if not results_path.exists():
    import importlib.util
    # If not yet created, execute analysis
    pass

with open(results_path, "rb") as f:
    results = pickle.load(f)

study = results["study"]
gaps = results["gaps"]
gpa_table = results["gpa_table"]
dropout_table = results["dropout_table"]

sleep_row = gpa_table.loc["sleep_hours"]
stress_row = dropout_table.loc["stress"]
support_row = dropout_table.loc["support"]

def format_p(p):
    return "p < .001" if p < 0.001 else f"p = {p:.3f}".replace(" 0.", " .")

def mean_sd(x):
    return f"{x.mean():.1f} ({x.std(ddof=1):.1f})"

def percent(x):
    return f"{100 * x.mean():.0f}%"
```

## Participants

The sample included `{python} len(study)` graduate students, `{python} int((study['programme'] == "Master's").sum())` in Master's and `{python} int((study['programme'] == 'PhD').sum())` in doctoral programmes (@tbl-sample).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-sample
#| tbl-cap: "Characteristics of the sample."
tbl = pd.DataFrame({
    "Characteristic": [
        "Age, mean (SD)", "Women", "Part-time",
        "Stress (1-5), mean (SD)", "Wellbeing in semester 1, mean (SD)"
    ],
    "Value": [
        mean_sd(study["age"]), percent(study["gender"] == "Female"),
        percent(study["study_mode"] == "Part-time"), mean_sd(study["stress"]),
        mean_sd(study["wellbeing"])
    ]
})
print(tbl.to_markdown(index=False))
```

## The wellbeing workshop

Wellbeing was similar in the two groups before the workshop (difference `{python} f"{gaps[1]:.1f}"` points). After the workshop, invited students' wellbeing was `{python} f"{gaps[2]:.1f}"` points higher in semester 2, but the difference narrowed to `{python} f"{gaps[3]:.1f}"` points in semester 3 and `{python} f"{gaps[4]:.1f}"` in semester 4 (@fig-results, panel A).

![(A) Predicted wellbeing by semester and workshop group. (B) First-semester GPA against hours of sleep.](output/figure-1.png){#fig-results fig-alt="Two panels: wellbeing by semester for the two workshop groups, and GPA against sleep with a regression line."}

## Grade point average

Each additional hour of sleep was associated with a GPA `{python} f"{sleep_row['estimate']:.2f}"` points higher (95% CI `{python} f"{sleep_row['conf_low']:.2f}"` to `{python} f"{sleep_row['conf_high']:.2f}"`, `{python} format_p(sleep_row['p_value'])`), holding study hours, stress, and support constant. The model explained `{python} f"{results['gpa_fit']['r_squared'] * 100:.0f}"`% of the variation in first-semester GPA.

## Considering dropping out

Each one-point increase in stress was associated with `{python} f"{stress_row['odds_ratio']:.1f}"` times the odds of considering dropping out (95% CI `{python} f"{stress_row['conf_low']:.1f}"` to `{python} f"{stress_row['conf_high']:.1f}"`), and each one-point increase in supervisor support with `{python} f"{support_row['odds_ratio']:.2f}"` times the odds (95% CI `{python} f"{support_row['conf_low']:.2f}"` to `{python} f"{support_row['conf_high']:.2f}"`). Effect sizes are interpreted following @cohen1988.
